LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we become better at spelling? 2. Why do we use abbreviations and acronyms in written texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy - self-awareness: The learners sort out their priorities as they search online or offline for examples of

abbreviations.

● Communication and collaboration - writing clearly: The learner advances the skill of spelling while designing charts and

posters featuring abbreviations, acronyms, words with affixes, frequently misspelt and easily confused words.

Values:
● Responsibility - diligence: The learner diligently uses the internet while searching for abbreviations and frequently

confused words.

● Patriotism: The learner respects classmates as they design charts and posters featuring abbreviations, acronyms, words

with affixes, frequently misspelt and easily confused words and display them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues - Climate change: The learner brings out issues on climate change in self-written paragraphs.
